literal: At the time Boling Cui Xiaofen, Fanyang Lu Daoyue, Longxi Li Zan and other daughters were all world wives.
idiomatic: At the time Boling Cui Xiaofen, Fanyang Lu Daoyue, Longxi Li Zan and other daughters were all world wives.

literal: All who sued were angrily reproached.
idiomatic: All who sued were angrily reproached.

literal: At the beginning of Wutai the empress had entered the Way; then she dwelt at Yaoguang Temple.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wutai the empress had entered the Way; then she dwelt at Yaoguang Temple.

literal: Xiaowu Empress Gao was Qi Shenwu's eldest daughter.
idiomatic: Xiaowu Empress Gao was Qi Shenwu's eldest daughter.

literal: When the emperor was established, she was taken as empress.
idiomatic: When the emperor was established, she was taken as empress.

literal: When the emperor went west to Guanzhong, she was demoted to consort of Prince of Pengcheng Shao.
idiomatic: When the emperor went west to Guanzhong, she was demoted to consort of Prince of Pengcheng Shao.

literal: Wendi Wen Empress Yifu was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
idiomatic: Wendi Wen Empress Yifu was a man of Luoyang in Henan.

literal: Her ancestors for generations were Tuyuhun chieftains, dwelling at Qinghai, titled King of Qinghai.
idiomatic: Her ancestors for generations were Tuyuhun chieftains, dwelling at Qinghai, titled King of Qinghai.

literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, the empress's great-grandfather Mogui led his tribe to submit; appointed Inspector of Dingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Xiping.
idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified, the empress's great-grandfather Mogui led his tribe to submit; appointed inspector of Dingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Xiping.

literal: From Mogui onward, three generations married princesses; daughters mostly became kings' consorts—greatly honored.
idiomatic: From Mogui onward, three generations married princesses; daughters mostly became kings' consorts—greatly honored.

literal: Father Yuan, Acting Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: Father Yuan, acting three excellencies, inspector of Yanzhou.

literal: Mother Princess of Huaiyang, Xiaowen's fourth daughter.
idiomatic: Mother Princess of Huaiyang, Xiaowen's fourth daughter.

literal: The empress had beautiful bearing; in youth little speech or laughter; her parents thought her unusual and showed relatives: "Bearing a daughter—what harm?
idiomatic: The empress had beautiful bearing; in youth little speech or laughter; her parents thought her unusual and showed relatives, "Bearing a daughter—what harm?

literal: If like this one, she truly surpasses a son."
idiomatic: If like this one, she truly surpasses a son."

literal: At sixteen Wendi took her as consort.
idiomatic: At sixteen Wendi took her as consort.

literal: When the emperor took the throne, in the first year of Datong she was enfeoffed empress.
idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, in the first year of Datong she was enfeoffed empress.

literal: The empress by nature loved frugality—vegetarian food and old clothes; pearls, jade, silk, and brocade were absent from dress and play.
idiomatic: The empress by nature loved frugality—vegetarian food and old clothes; pearls, jade, silk, and brocade were absent from dress and play.

literal: Also humane and forgiving without a jealous heart—the emperor further valued her.
idiomatic: Also humane and forgiving without a jealous heart—the emperor further valued her.

literal: She bore sons and daughters twelve; most died young—only the crown prince and Prince of Wudu Wu survived.
idiomatic: She bore sons and daughters twelve; most died young—only the crown prince and Prince of Wudu Wu survived.

literal: At the time the new capital was in Guanzhong; eager to campaign east, Rouran raided the border—northern campaign was not yet possible; therefore the emperor made marriage to soothe them.
idiomatic: At the time the new capital was in Guanzhong; eager to campaign east, Rouran raided the border—northern campaign was not yet possible; therefore the emperor made marriage to soothe them.

literal: Then he further took in the Dao empress; he ordered the empress to yield dwelling in a separate palace and leave home as a nun.
idiomatic: Then he further took in the Dao empress; he ordered the empress to yield dwelling in a separate palace and leave home as a nun.

literal: The Dao empress still harbored suspicion; again moved the empress to dwell in Qinzhou, relying on her son, Inspector of Qinzhou Prince of Wudu.
idiomatic: The Dao empress still harbored suspicion; again moved the empress to dwell in Qinzhou, relying on her son, inspector of Qinzhou Prince of Wudu.

literal: Though the emperor was bound by the great plan, fondness was not forgotten; afterward he secretly ordered her hair nurtured—there was intent to recall.
idiomatic: Though the emperor was bound by the great plan, fondness was not forgotten; afterward he secretly ordered her hair nurtured—there was intent to recall.

literal: Yet the affair was secret and forbidden; outwardly none knew.
idiomatic: Yet the affair was secret and forbidden; outwardly none knew.

literal: In the sixth year spring, Rouran led the state across the river; the vanguard had already passed Xia; many said the barbarians rose this campaign because of the Dao empress.
idiomatic: In the sixth year spring, Rouran led the state across the river; the vanguard had already passed Xia; many said the barbarians rose this campaign because of the Dao empress.

literal: The emperor said: "How could a million host be raised for one woman?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "How could a million host be raised for one woman?

literal: Even so, to produce this talk—what face have I to see the generals!"
idiomatic: Even so, to produce this talk—what face have I to see the generals!"

literal: Then he sent Palace Attendant Cao Chong with hand edict ordering the empress to end herself.
idiomatic: Then he sent Palace Attendant Cao Chong with hand edict ordering the empress to end herself.

literal: The empress received the edict, brushed tears and told Chong: "May the Supreme Ultimate enjoy ten thousand years, the realm peaceful and secure—I die without regret."
idiomatic: The empress received the edict, brushed tears and told Chong, "May the Supreme Ultimate enjoy ten thousand years, the realm peaceful and secure—I die without regret."

literal: She then ordered Prince of Wudu forward to part with him.
idiomatic: She then ordered Prince of Wudu forward to part with him.

literal: She left words for the crown prince—words all mournful; she wept bitterly long.
idiomatic: She left words for the crown prince—words all mournful; she wept bitterly long.

literal: Attendants all shed tears and lost voice; none could look up.
idiomatic: Attendees all shed tears and lost voice; none could look up.

literal: She summoned monks to set offerings; ordered several tens of maidservants to leave home; hair fell from their hands.
idiomatic: She summoned monks to set offerings; ordered several tens of maidservants to leave home; hair fell from their hands.

literal: When the affair was done, she entered the chamber, pulled the coverlet over herself and died, age thirty-one.
idiomatic: When the affair was done, she entered the chamber, pulled the coverlet over herself and died, age thirty-one.

literal: Maijiji Cliff was carved for a niche and burial; as the spirit coffin entered, two cloud clusters first entered the niche—soon one vanished and one emerged; her mound title was Jiling.
idiomatic: Maijiji Cliff was carved for a niche and burial; as the spirit coffin entered, two cloud clusters first entered the niche—soon one vanished and one emerged; her mound title was Jiling.

literal: When Wendi's mountain tomb was finished, a hand writ said: after ten thousand years wish military paired sacrifice.
idiomatic: When Wendi's mountain tomb was finished, a hand writ said: after ten thousand years wish military paired sacrifice.

literal: Dukes and ministers then debated posthumous title Wen Empress, attached at the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: Dukes and ministers then debated posthumous title Wen Empress, attached at the Grand Temple.

literal: Under the Deposed Emperor, joint burial at Yong Tomb.
idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor, joint burial at Yong Tomb.

literal: Wendi Dao Empress Yujiulü was eldest daughter of Rouran lord Anagui.
idiomatic: Wendi Dao Empress Yujiulü was eldest daughter of Rouran lord Anagui.

literal: Bearing and appearance proper and stern; from youth had mature wisdom.
idiomatic: Bearing and appearance proper and stern; from youth had mature wisdom.

literal: At the beginning of Datong, Rouran repeatedly encroached the northern border; Wendi then made treaty, friendly marriage; Prince of Fufeng Fu received commission to welcome.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong, Rouran repeatedly encroached the northern border; Wendi then made treaty, friendly marriage; Prince of Fufeng Fu received commission to welcome.

literal: By Rouran custom the east was honored; when the empress came, camp tents and mats all faced east.
idiomatic: By Rouran custom the east was honored; when the empress came, camp tents and mats all faced east.

literal: Seven hundred carts, ten thousand horses, a thousand camels.
idiomatic: Seven hundred carts, ten thousand horses, a thousand camels.

literal: At Black Salt Pool, Wei court insignia and regalia first arrived.
idiomatic: At Black Salt Pool, Wei court insignia and regalia first arrived.

literal: Fu memorialized requesting to face south; the empress said: "I have not seen the Wei lord—thus I am still a Rouran woman.
idiomatic: Fu memorialized requesting to face south; the empress said, "I have not seen the Wei lord—thus I am still a Rouran woman.

literal: Wei arms face south—I myself face east."
idiomatic: Wei arms face south—I myself face east."

literal: Fu had no words.
idiomatic: Fu had no words.

literal: In the first month of the fourth year she reached the capital; established empress, age fourteen.
idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year she reached the capital; established empress, age fourteen.

literal: In the sixth year the empress was pregnant and about to bear; she dwelt at Yaohua Hall; hearing dogs bark above, her heart greatly hated it.
idiomatic: In the sixth year the empress was pregnant and about to bear; she dwelt at Yaohua Hall; hearing dogs bark above, her heart greatly hated it.

literal: Also she saw a woman in full adornment come to the empress's place; the empress asked attendants: "Who is this person?"
idiomatic: Also she saw a woman in full adornment come to the empress's place; the empress asked attendants, "Who is this person?"

literal: Physicians and shamans at the side—all none saw; at the time it was thought Wen Empress's spirit.
idiomatic: Physicians and shamans at the side—all none saw; at the time it was thought Wen Empress's spirit.

literal: When bearing was finished she died, age sixteen; buried at Shaoling Plain.
idiomatic: When bearing was finished she died, age sixteen; buried at Shaoling Plain.

literal: In the seventeenth year, joint burial at Yong Tomb.
idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, joint burial at Yong Tomb.

literal: When meeting at Heng Bridge north, the empress's inner coffin first reached Deer Park; the emperor's hearse came after; about to reach the resting place—the shaft broke and would not advance.
idiomatic: When meeting at Heng Bridge north, the empress's inner coffin first reached Deer Park; the emperor's hearse came after; about to reach the resting place—the shaft broke and would not advance.

literal: Gongdi Empress Ruogan was daughter of Minister of Works Duke of Changle Zheng Hui.
idiomatic: Gongdi Empress Ruogan was daughter of Minister of Works Duke of Changle Zheng Hui.

literal: She had bearing and color; Gongdi took her as consort.
idiomatic: She had bearing and color; Gongdi took her as consort.

literal: When he took the throne, she was established empress.
idiomatic: When he took the throne, she was established empress.

literal: Later she left home as a nun; she died in a Buddhist temple—ultimately no posthumous title.
idiomatic: Later she left home as a nun; she died in a Buddhist temple—ultimately no posthumous title.

literal: Xiaojing Empress Gao was Qi Shenwu's second daughter.
idiomatic: Xiaojing Empress Gao was Qi Shenwu's second daughter.

literal: In the fourth year of Tianping an edict betrothed her as empress; Shenwu before and after firmly declined—the emperor did not permit.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianping an edict betrothed her as empress; Shenwu before and after firmly declined—the emperor did not permit.

literal: At the beginning of Xinghe, edict ordered Minister of State Sun Teng, Minister of Works Prince of Xiangcheng Chang and others to bear edict and perform ritual; the empress was welcomed by carriage from the chancellor's residence at Jinyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xinghe, edict ordered Minister of State Sun Teng, Minister of Works Prince of Xiangcheng Chang and others to bear edict and perform ritual; the empress was welcomed by carriage from the chancellor's residence at Jinyang.

literal: In the fifth month she was established empress; great amnesty.
idiomatic: In the fifth month she was established empress; great amnesty.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, she was demoted to consort of Prince of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, she was demoted to consort of Prince of Zhongshan.

literal: The empress married Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Zunyan.
idiomatic: The empress married Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Zunyan.
